text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- Fourth day of clashes in the West Bank and Gaza. Israeli reinforcements in case the confrontation broadens. Washington rejects condemnation of Israel, while France holds Israel responsible for the outbreak of violence.
- Washington offers to host an Arab-Israeli summit as soon as possible. The Palestinians prefer to hold the Arafat-Netanyahu meeting in Cairo with Mubarak present.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa had a telephone conversation yesterday evening with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, who had a call from U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
- Mubarak will receive Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Thursday during Erbakan's two-day visit.

- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib announced that more measures will be taken in favour of investors and exporters and to bring about reconciliation between taxpayers and the tax department. The plan for tax on entertainment will be reviewed.
AL-AKHBAR

- Contacts are still under way on the time and venue for the expected summit between Arafat and Netanhayu. Diplomatic sources in New York said Christopher and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette may take part in the summit. Contacts are also underway to arrange a meeting between Arafat and Netanyahu in Hebron before the summit, which might place on Monday.
- Cotton export prices will be announced today for the third week of the season and Trade and Supply Minister Ahmed Gueily said prices would move according to the world market.
- President Mubarak delegates Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi to lay a wreath at the tomb of Gamal Abdel Nasser on the 26th anniversary of the late president's death.
- Culture Minister Farouk Hosni opened the Dahshour area to tourists for the first time after two years' work developing and renovating the area.
- A report said Major Muawwad Abu Galil, the police officer kiled at Rafah last week, was hit with a dumdum bullet fired by Israeli soldiers.
AL-GOMHURIA
- The United States has suggested an Arafat-Netanyahu summit in Washington. Arafat wants a detailed agenda and has rejected a proposal that he first meet Netanyahu at the Erez crossing.
- Presidential adviser Osama el-Baz said the policies adopted by current Israeli government are a residue of the security theory which the 1973 war undermined.
- Twenty-eight bodies have now been recovered from the accident in which a Nile ferry sank last Thursday.
- Demonstrations inside Cairo University on Saturday in protest at Israeli behaviour towards Palestinians.
- A Palestinian police unit took over the border post on the border between Egypt and the Gaza Strip and raised the Palestinian flag on it.
